# [SECTION 01]{.kicker}Why it matters {.divider background-color="#530153"}

## Surveys are intensive. AI can help, but value is not automatic.

::: {.sub}
The question is not where AI can be inserted. It is where AI creates the most useful and equitable return.
:::

::: {.grid3}
::: {.card}
::: {.cardhead}
[T]{.letter} TIME
:::

Repeated drafting, programming, translation, testing, supervision and cleaning consume scarce staff time.
:::

::: {.card}
::: {.cardhead}
[Q]{.letter} QUALITY
:::

Errors can propagate across the workflow and may only become visible after fieldwork begins.
:::

::: {.card}
::: {.cardhead}
[C]{.letter} COST
:::

AI can reduce some tasks, but brings tool, review, infrastructure, privacy and skills costs.
:::
:::

::: {.caveat .purple}
**TEAM DECISION** Prioritize the use cases with the highest time or quality value-add, then assess whether benefits and costs are distributed equitably.
:::

::: {.notes}
Invite the team to name one bottleneck that absorbs significant time, and one group that might be disadvantaged by the proposed AI use.
:::

## [STAGE 1 OF 5 | DESIGN, PILOTING AND TRANSLATION]{.stagelabel}Design, piloting, and translation

::: {.sub}
Use AI to accelerate the first draft, not to declare the instrument finished.
:::

:::: {.cols}
::: {.support}
::: {.colhead .green}
HOW AI CAN SUPPORT
:::

- Synthesize literature and locate outcomes and measurement frameworks
- Find tested questions in standard questionnaires and the DIME questionnaire database
- Review question wording for common measurement errors and propose unbiased alternatives
- Expand desk testing: generate test scenarios and assess cognitive burden across respondent profiles
- Translate into common languages with available AI models, for expert review
:::

::: {.resources}
::: {.colhead .purple}
RESOURCES
:::

::: {.res}
[AI translation]{.res-name}[AVAILABLE]{.pill .avail}

Available AI models handle common languages well. Local languages remain the open question.
:::

::: {.res}
[Question database]{.res-name}[IN THE WORKS]{.pill .works}

App built on standard questionnaires and the DIME questionnaire database.
:::
:::
::::

::: {.caveat}
**CAVEAT** Check every question and translation thoroughly before field use. Value comparability and existing best practices.
:::

::: {.notes}
Emphasize that AI accelerates iteration. It does not remove the need for subject-matter or language expertise. The original piloting content had no tool in progress, so piloting appears here as AI support only; synthetic testing sits under programming and testing.
:::

## [STAGE 2 OF 5 | PROGRAMMING AND TESTING]{.stagelabel}Programming and testing

::: {.sub}
From paper to a working, tested form faster.
:::

:::: {.cols}
::: {.support}
::: {.colhead .green}
HOW AI CAN SUPPORT
:::

- Convert paper questionnaires to XLSForm. AI tools like Claude do this well
- Accelerate survey coding with agents and reusable skills
- Enumerate pathways and flag rare questions, loops and inconsistent constraints
- Generate synthetic response combinations to test skip logic before fieldwork
:::

::: {.resources}
::: {.colhead .purple}
RESOURCES
:::

::: {.res}
[SurveyCTO skill]{.res-name}[AVAILABLE]{.pill .avail}

SurveyCTO's AI agent skill for designing and debugging forms. [Link](https://www.surveycto.com/?p=47097)
:::

::: {.res}
[Paper-to-XLSForm converter]{.res-name}[DRAFT]{.pill .draft}

Draft skill that turns a paper questionnaire into an XLSForm.
:::

::: {.res}
[XLSForm consolidator]{.res-name}[DRAFT]{.pill .draft}

Draft skill. [Describe what it consolidates]
:::

::: {.res}
[Synthetic testing]{.res-name}[IN THE WORKS]{.pill .works}

Synthetic respondents run through the programmed SurveyCTO form.
:::
:::
::::

::: {.caveat}
**CAVEAT** Check every programmed constraint before field use. Synthetic respondents complement, rather than replace, field pilots.
:::

::: {.notes}
Hand over to the demo section for the XLSForm part. Feedback on the draft skills is very helpful as the team tests them.
:::

## [STAGE 3 OF 5 | RESPONSE COLLECTION AND FIELD WORK MANAGEMENT]{.stagelabel}Response collection and field work management

::: {.sub}
AI can support both the interview channel and the management layer.
:::

:::: {.cols}
::: {.support}
::: {.colhead .green}
HOW AI CAN SUPPORT
:::

- Draft terms of reference for survey firms
- Generate enumerator manuals tailored to the instrument
- AI-powered adaptive training and simulation for enumerator preparation
- AI-agent data collection through IVR or chatbots
- Synthesize GPS and completion rates to help field managers target follow-up
:::

::: {.resources}
::: {.colhead .purple}
RESOURCES
:::

::: {.res}
[ToR generator]{.res-name}[DRAFT]{.pill .draft}

Draft skill for terms of reference.
:::

::: {.res}
[Enumerator manual generator]{.res-name}[DRAFT]{.pill .draft}

Draft skill for enumerator manuals.
:::

::: {.res}
[IVR and chatbots]{.res-name}[PARTNERS]{.pill .partner}

LSMS pilots on the Resonance platform in Nepal and Bangladesh.
:::
:::
::::

::: {.caveat}
**CAVEAT** Mode effects, accessibility, consent and respondent trust must be assessed before deployment.
:::

::: {.notes}
Feedback on the draft skills is very helpful as the team tests them.
:::

## [STAGE 4 OF 5 | DATA QUALITY CHECKS]{.stagelabel}Data quality checks during fieldwork

::: {.sub}
Move from delayed review of a sample toward faster, targeted quality signals.
:::

:::: {.cols}
::: {.support}
::: {.colhead .green}
HOW AI CAN SUPPORT
:::

- Transcribe and review recorded interviews
- Set up back check instruments
- Detect irregular patterns, protocol deviations and faulty responses
- Prioritize interviews for supervisor review
- Generate concise, actionable quality summaries
:::

::: {.resources}
::: {.colhead .purple}
RESOURCES
:::

::: {.res}
[iehfc]{.res-name}[AVAILABLE]{.pill .avail}

High-frequency checks tools developed by the DECDI team.
:::

::: {.res}
[Skill from DJ]{.res-name}[DRAFT]{.pill .draft}

[Describe what it does and confirm status]
:::

::: {.res}
[Audio audits]{.res-name}[PARTNERS]{.pill .partner}

Automated transcription pipeline trialed by LSMS in several countries.
:::
:::
::::

::: {.caveat}
**CAVEAT** AI flags are signals for review, not proof of fraud or poor performance.
:::

::: {.notes}
Show how iehfc, the skill from DJ and the LSMS audio audit work fit together rather than overlap.
:::

## [STAGE 5 OF 5 | DATA CLEANING AND PUBLICATION]{.stagelabel}Data cleaning and publication

::: {.sub}
Codify recurring workflows so teams spend less time rebuilding routine steps.
:::

:::: {.cols}
::: {.support}
::: {.colhead .green}
HOW AI CAN SUPPORT
:::

- Clean up scripts, create codebooks, and provide descriptions
- Classify and summarize open-ended responses
- Create reusable skills for standard checks and outputs
- Support documentation and disclosure risk checks
:::

::: {.resources}
::: {.colhead .purple}
RESOURCES
:::

Cleaning scripts and reproducible reports. DECDI starting point.
:::

::: {.res}

De-identification review before release. [Partner: MDL, to confirm]
:::

::: {.res}
[Catalog checklist]{.res-name}[UPCOMING]{.pill .next}

Step-by-step support for Microdata Catalog submission.
:::
:::
::::

::: {.caveat}
**CAVEAT** Keep code, prompts, model versions and human decisions auditable and reproducible.
:::

::: {.notes}
Nothing is built yet at this stage. These are the next skills on the workplan.

# [SECTION 04]{.kicker}Choosing where to start {.divider background-color="#530153"}

## How to choose where to start

::: {.sub}
Prioritize a workflow problem, not an AI tool.
:::

::: {.grid2}
::: {.card}
::: {.cardhead}
[V]{.letter} VALUE
:::

How much staff time, delay or quality loss does the current problem create?
:::

::: {.card}
::: {.cardhead}
[F]{.letter} FEASIBILITY
:::

Are the data, infrastructure, language coverage and staff skills available?
:::

::: {.card}
::: {.cardhead}
[E]{.letter} EQUITY
:::

Who benefits, who may be excluded, and who bears additional review or participation costs?
:::

::: {.card}
::: {.cardhead}
[R]{.letter} RISK
:::

What happens if the output is wrong, biased, insecure or misunderstood?
:::
:::

# [SECTION 05]{.kicker}Safeguards and closing {.divider background-color="#530153"}

## Caveats when embedding AI in survey workflows

::: {.sub}
Build safeguards into the workflow rather than adding them after deployment.
:::

::: {.grid3}
::: {.card}
::: {.cardhead}
[H]{.letter} HUMAN ACCOUNTABILITY
:::

Assign a named reviewer and define decisions that cannot be automated.
:::

::: {.card}
::: {.cardhead}
[V]{.letter} VALIDATION
:::

Benchmark outputs against expert review and field evidence in the intended context.
:::

::: {.card}
::: {.cardhead}
[E]{.letter} EQUITY & LANGUAGE
:::

Test performance across languages, modes, locations and respondent groups.
:::

::: {.card}
::: {.cardhead}
[P]{.letter} PRIVACY & CONSENT
:::

Minimize sensitive data, explain AI use and secure audio, text and location data.
:::

::: {.card}
::: {.cardhead}
[R]{.letter} REPRODUCIBILITY
:::

Record prompts, versions, code, inputs, changes and human overrides.
:::

::: {.card}
::: {.cardhead}
[T]{.letter} TOTAL COST
:::

Include licenses, compute, connectivity, integration, review, training and maintenance.
:::
:::

::: {.caveat .purple}
**DEFAULT POSTURE** Pilot narrowly, review visibly, monitor continuously and retain a non-AI fallback.
:::

::: {.notes}
Full reproducibility is not easy to achieve in the end.
:::
